h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ט׳ Motzei Yom Kippur, 9
"Hashem Is My Light and My Salvation": Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Sukkos

p: "Of David: Hashem is my light and my salvation"
And it is brought in the Midrash
"Hashem is my light" on Rosh Hashanah,
For behold, it is brought in the Tikkunim
as it says, 'And it was the day';
"this is the day, the beginning of Your works,"
and concerning the very beginning of the creation of light
However, in order for it to flow
in this world to the recipient,
it must come about through contraction,
and this is on the day of Rosh Hashanah,
And for this He gives Yisrael the counsel,
on the day of Rosh Hashanah,
in order "to arouse that supernal shofar"
"they walk in the light of Your countenance"
as it was at the Giving of the Torah,
when there were illuminations of revelation
through "the sound of a very powerful shofar"
And just as in the future to come there will be
the revelation of His light, may He be blessed, in completeness,
"And it shall be on that day
that a great shofar will be blown"
And this is "Hashem is my light" on Rosh Hashanah.
as is brought in the Raya Mehemna
to bring accusation, and so on;
of the dew of heaven," etc.
"And it was, as Yaakov had just gone out,
that Esav his brother came in from his hunt"
he raised a number of claims in order to accuse,
as is brought in the holy Zohar
when He gives him the gift, the goat.
And this is "and my salvation" on Yom Kippur,
the revelation of the salvation in actuality.
"Hashem is the stronghold of my life"
this alludes to the festival of Sukkos,
when the might and the strength are completed
through the Season of our Rejoicing,
as is brought in the holy Zohar
that the Holy One, blessed be He,
and through this He gives strength
"For the joy of Hashem is your strength"
and it is brought in the Midrash as well
(שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב שָׁם; וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ד)
"With this shall Aharon come into the Sanctuary"
of the revelation of the Kingship of Heaven
and it is called Knesses Yisrael,
as the holy Zohar puts it
and clear before a person's eyes,
and "zos" is in the feminine aspect,
when it is received in the souls of Yisrael.
And the revelation of this bond
for all the days of the year.
And it is brought in the Midrash on Parshas Acharei
on the verse "With this shall Aharon come,"
which correspond to the ten sefiros.
they correspond to the first three sefiros,
are the very essence of Yisrael's bond
with Hashem, may He be blessed,
something with which none of the nations
For Torah may not be taught to a gentile,
"and His ordinances they have not known"
(תְּהִלִּים קמז, כ; וְעַיֵּן סַנְהֶדְרִין נט, א).
And milah is only for the seed of Yisrael,
as is known, that uncircumcised Jews
which is not so of circumcised idolaters
And Shabbos: it is known that a gentile who keeps Shabbos
In all these, as though pointed out with a finger,
because Hashem, may He be blessed,
dwells in the depths of their hearts.
And afterwards come the last seven,

inlineHeadings.text: Light on Rosh Hashanah, salvation on Yom Kippur
"And there was light": an expression of distress
The shofar draws the light down
The light concealed: Yaakov and Esav
"In this I trust": the ten things called "zos"
Torah, milah and Shabbos: Yisrael's own

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tehillim 27 — "The Rabbis interpret the verses as Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: 'my light' — on Rosh Hashanah; 'and my salvation' — on Yom Kippur… The Satan in gematria is 364: all the days of the year he has permission to accuse, except on Yom Kippur… 'In this (be-zos) I trust' — Rabbi Levi said: … 'With this (be-zos) shall Aharon come into the Sanctuary' (Vayikra 16:3)."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 36 (77b) — "'Let there be light' — this is Pesach, the night [or] of the fourteenth; 'and there was light' — Rosh Hashanah, of which it is said 'and it was [vayehi] the day'; here vayehi and there vayehi, and everywhere vayehi is a term of distress." Or l'arba'ah asar is the Mishnah's term for the night of the fourteenth (Pesachim 2a).

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 99b (Emor) — "'At the covered time for our festival day' (Tehillim 81:4) — when the moon is covered… And with what does all shine? With teshuvah and with the sound of the shofar, as it is written, 'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah; Hashem, in the light of Your countenance they shall walk' (Tehillim 89:16)."

paragraphs.text: Raaya Mehemna, Zohar III 99b–100a (Emor) — "'And Yitzchak trembled exceedingly' (Bereishis 27:33)… 'who is he that hunted game' — through many prayers and supplications…" And Yaakov goes through the days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur fleeing to be saved from him, returning in teshuvah and fasting; for Israel know that Esav comes with four hundred men, all of them accusers ready to accuse them.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 59a — "Rabbi Yochanan said: An idolater who occupies himself with Torah is liable to death, as it says, 'Moshe commanded us the Torah, an inheritance (morashah) of the congregation of Yaakov' (Devarim 33:4) — an inheritance for us and not for them." The Gemara also reads it me'orasah, "betrothed."
